points.description: States that when bulb A burns out the circuit is broken/open, so there is no longer a complete (closed) path for current through B, C and the battery, so no current flows and B and C go out. Equivalent wording accepted (e.g. A is in series with B and C, so the break stops current to both).

rubric.notes: Full mark for explaining that the burned-out A breaks the only closed path containing B, C and the battery, so no current flows through them. No mark for just saying 'A is broken' or 'they are connected' without mentioning the loss of a complete path/current.
